newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Shenzhen B shares lower on falls in weak stocks.
newsitem.headline: Shenzhen B shares lower on falls in weak stocks.

text.p: Shenzhen's B share index closed slightly lower on Monday, reversing early gains late in the session due in part to selling of weaker shares, brokers said.
The B share index shed 0.18 points, or 0.20 percent, to 90.67 on turnover of HK$13.57 million, compared with HK$14.71 million on Monday.

Some investors were seen reducing positions in cheap issues likely to report weak 1996 results and putting the money into shares like Fangda and Gujing that promise good earnings as the year-end approaches, brokers said.
Television maker Huafa, the worst performer, slumped HK$0.09, or 5.29 percent, to HK$1.61, on volume of 52,800 shares. Nanshan Power Station dipped HK$0.10, or 4.39 percent, to HK$2.18.
Dadonghai traded the most on volume of 673,500 shares and closed off HK$0.01 at HK$1.32.
Weifu, the best performing counter, surged HK$0.32 or 10.60 percent, to HK$3.34, with only 7,600 shares changing hands.

The Shenzhen-based Securities Times said on Monday that Weifu, which makes auto parts, had so far this year received orders worth about 800 million yuan for delivery in 1997, which will greatly improve the company's performance.
Fangda, which fell sharply on Friday, rebounded HK$0.16, or 3.70 percent, to HK$4.49 on trade of 429,900 shares.
Gujing rose HK$0.20 to HK$6.20, in trade of 442,816 shares, making it the day's second most active counter.

The A share market rebounded strongly on Monday following Friday's plunge, with the index firming 8.12 points, or 2.13 percent, to 388.72. The composite index finished up 7.28 points, or 2.05 percent, at 361.78.
Turnover shrank to 8.27 billion yuan from 11.52 billion on Friday.
Institutional buying was focused on high-priced issues, brokers said.
Huali High-tech soared 1.77 yuan, or 10.91 percent, to 18.00 yuan and steel pipe maker Ningbo Zhongyuan jumped 1.44 yuan, or 9.99 percent, to 15.85 yuan.
